name: cardgame-lib-markdown-section-parser-dedup
title: Extract the duplicated H2/H3-section-splitting and paragraph-extraction helpers shared by cardGame's 4 newer lib/parse-*-markdown.js files into one shared module
pitch: lib/parse-race-markdown.js and lib/parse-lore-markdown.js each define a byte-identical splitIntoH2Sections; lib/parse-star-atlas-markdown.js and lib/parse-founts-markdown.js each define a byte-identical splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent; extractParagraph's blank-line-join logic and (in 2 of the 4) a redundant local slugify are copy-pasted across all four files — dedup this before a future 6th domain parser copies it again.
why_now: Verified live by reading all 4 files in full: lib/parse-race-markdown.js lines 17-36 and lib/parse-lore-markdown.js lines 21-40 contain the identical splitIntoH2Sections function, down to the same regex and a comment in each explicitly referencing the other as the source of the convention. lib/parse-star-atlas-markdown.js lines 23-46 and lib/parse-founts-markdown.js lines 19-42 contain the identical splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent function, same comment-cross-reference pattern. extractParagraph (trim non-blank lines, join with a space) appears near-verbatim in all four files (parse-race-markdown.js:45-50, parse-star-atlas-markdown.js:72-76, parse-lore-markdown.js:58-61, parse-founts-markdown.js:58-62). Additionally, parse-race-markdown.js:142-147 and parse-star-atlas-markdown.js:103-108 each re-declare their own slugify instead of importing the one lib/parse-card-markdown.js already exports, which parse-lore-markdown.js and parse-founts-markdown.js already do correctly — a fourth duplication, and an inconsistency between otherwise-identical files. This is the exact shape of the three previously shipped dedup units (cardgame-tools-loader-dedup, cardgame-tools-shared-parser-dedup, cardgame-tools-fs-lock-dedup), applied to lib/ files none of those touched. None of the 5 currently window-open proposals (design-readiness section4/gap3 doc fixes, art-briefs-spatial-race-identity-wave-2, jaina-sync-tools-dedup, both playtest refreshes) reference any lib/parse-*-markdown.js file or design/races.md, design/star-atlas.md, design/lore.md, or design/world.md — checked memory and every open proposal first per T24.
expected_outcome: A new lib/markdown-sections.js exports splitIntoH2Sections, splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent, and extractParagraph; lib/parse-race-markdown.js, lib/parse-star-atlas-markdown.js, lib/parse-lore-markdown.js, and lib/parse-founts-markdown.js each import these three helpers, plus slugify from lib/parse-card-markdown.js, instead of re-implementing any of them. Each parser's own existing test suite passes unmodified, and calling loadAllRaces(), loadAllWorlds(), loadAllEras(), and loadAllFounts() against the real design/ files returns output identical to before the refactor.
intent: Four of cardGame's lib/parse-*-markdown.js domain parsers — parse-race-markdown.js, parse-star-atlas-markdown.js, parse-lore-markdown.js, and parse-founts-markdown.js — were each written to parse a different design/ file, but they hand-roll the same three low-level building blocks. splitIntoH2Sections (walk lines, track the current level-2-heading section, push non-heading lines into it) is copy-pasted verbatim between parse-race-markdown.js and parse-lore-markdown.js. splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent (the same walk, but for level-3 headings, additionally remembering the nearest preceding level-2 heading so callers can tell which group a record fell under) is copy-pasted verbatim between parse-star-atlas-markdown.js and parse-founts-markdown.js. extractParagraph (trim each line, drop blanks, join the rest with a single space) is copy-pasted, with only cosmetic parameter differences, across all four files. And slugify (lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs to a single hyphen, trim leading/trailing hyphens) is redeclared locally in parse-race-markdown.js and parse-star-atlas-markdown.js even though lib/parse-card-markdown.js already exports the identical function and parse-lore-markdown.js/parse-founts-markdown.js already import it from there instead of redeclaring it. Add lib/markdown-sections.js exporting splitIntoH2Sections, splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent, and extractParagraph exactly as currently implemented (no behavior change — same regexes, same trimming, same return shapes), then update all four parser files to import these three functions from it and to import slugify from lib/parse-card-markdown.js, deleting each file's own now-redundant copy. Do not change any parser's public exports, field names, record shape, or the markdown convention it parses (H1-per-file for races, H2-Timeline-of-Eras-driven ordering for lore, H2/H3-parent-tagged for star-atlas and founts) — this unit only moves duplicated internals into one place, it does not touch design/races/, design/star-atlas.md, design/lore.md, design/world.md, or any tool that calls these parsers.

criteria.text: lib/markdown-sections.js exists and exports splitIntoH2Sections, splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent, and extractParagraph; lib/parse-race-markdown.js and lib/parse-lore-markdown.js both import splitIntoH2Sections from it instead of defining their own copy; lib/parse-star-atlas-markdown.js and lib/parse-founts-markdown.js both import splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent from it instead of defining their own copy

All four parser files import extractParagraph from lib/markdown-sections.js instead of each defining its own version, and lib/parse-race-markdown.js and lib/parse-star-atlas-markdown.js both import slugify from lib/parse-card-markdown.js instead of redeclaring it locally
Each of the four parser modules' own existing test suite passes unmodified against the refactored code

Calling loadAllRaces(), loadAllWorlds(), loadAllEras(), and loadAllFounts() against the real design/ files after the refactor returns the same records in the same order with the same field values as calling them did before the refactor
lib/markdown-sections.js has its own direct unit test exercising splitIntoH2Sections, splitIntoH3SectionsWithParent, and extractParagraph independent of any of the four domain parsers
